findings.title: User-level download/upload over plain HTTP enables tampering of downloaded level content
findings.entry_point: MyTreasureUserlevelsLoad.load(), invoked from MyTreasurePanel.loadUserlevels() background thread (MyTreasurePanel.java:390-398) on app start; response body lines become the playable user levels
findings.sink: java.net.URL.openConnection() against http://www.apo-games.de/myTreasure/get_level.php (load, line 190) and save_level.php (save, line 149)
findings.data_path: MyTreasureActivity.onCreateApp -> MyTreasurePanel.init() (line 142) -> loadUserlevels() Thread -> MyTreasureUserLevels.loadUserlevels() (MyTreasureUserLevels.java:47-62) -> MyTreasureUserlevelsLoad.load() -> URLConnection over cleartext HTTP; response lines parsed into lists (lines 207-235) and stored into MyTreasureLevels.editorLevels (MyTreasureUserLevels.java:55)
findings.attack_scenario: Attacker on the same LAN / captive portal / ISP intercepts the HTTP GET to get_level.php and rewrites the response lines. The injected strings are subsequently parsed by MyTreasureGame.loadLevel (see finding 02) and rendered as level names/statistics, giving the attacker full control of the content pipeline that feeds the level parser. Uploads (editor 'upload' button -> MyTreasureEditor.uploadString() line 251 -> save()) equally expose the submitted level string in cleartext.
findings.preconditions: Device online (isOnline() gate, MyTreasureActivity.java:42-47); attacker positioned on-path (no TLS, no pinning, no certificate logic anywhere in the variant).
findings.validation_plan: Run the app with a proxy (mitmproxy on adb reverse or Wi-Fi gateway). Observe plaintext 'POST /myTreasure/get_level.php HTTP/1.1' and 'POST .../save_level.php' with form body 'level=...'. Return a modified multi-line body (11 lines per level: level-string, time, counts...) and verify the injected level appears in Menu > 'userlevels' chooser and is playable.

findings.title: Server-supplied level strings parsed by hand with substring()/Integer.valueOf() and no validation -> remotely triggerable crash
findings.code_excerpt: this.level[y][x] = Integer.valueOf(levelString.substring(y * this.level[0].length + x + 4, y * this.level[0].length + x + 5));
findings.entry_point: HTTP response lines from get_level.php stored in MyTreasureLevels.editorLevels; selected via MyTreasureLevelChooser.touchedReleased (MyTreasureLevelChooser.java:237-239) -> MyTreasurePanel.setGame(true,false,i,"") (MyTreasurePanel.java:283) -> MyTreasureGame.loadLevel
findings.sink: Integer.valueOf(levelString.substring(...)) at MyTreasureGame.java:175-178 and 186, and array allocation new int[j*2][i] at line 180, all driven by attacker-controlled characters
findings.data_path: loadLevel(false, i, "") -> bUserLevel branch (lines 139-151) sets levelString=editorLevels[level] -> gold/silver parsed from last 4 chars (175-176), width i and height j from first 4 chars (177-178), arrays sized (180), cells parsed char-by-char (183-191). Any non-digit -> NumberFormatException; declared i*j larger than supplied payload -> StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. Also re-entered from think() line 286 when level[0][0]==-1 (restart/next-level), so the exception fires inside the update/render loop.
findings.attack_scenario: An anonymous party POSTs a malformed 'level' line to save_level.php (protocol accepts anything, see finding 04) or a network attacker modifies the get_level.php response (finding 01), e.g. first line '9999' (declares 99x99 grid but supplies no cell data) or '0a06...'. Every player who taps that level in the user-level chooser gets an uncaught NumberFormatException/StringIndexOutOfBoundsException on the game thread and the process dies (FATAL EXCEPTION in logcat). Effect: persistent remote DoS of the app for all players until the server entry is removed. Note the blast radius is bounded: width/height are only two digits (max 99x99, ~78 KB allocation), so no OOM vector exists.
findings.preconditions: Attacker-controlled level string reaches editorLevels (via scripted anonymous upload to save_level.php or on-path HTTP tampering); victim browses user levels and opens the crafted one.
findings.validation_plan: Two ways: (a) mitmproxy the get_level.php response so the first returned level line is '9999'; tap the first user level in-app; observe AndroidRuntime FATAL EXCEPTION StringIndexOutOfBoundsException in MyTreasureGame.loadLevel via adb logcat. (b) curl -d 'level=9999' http://www.apo-games.de/myTreasure/save_level.php from any host, refresh user levels in the app, select the new level, same crash.

findings.title: Deduplication check substrings every server-provided level string; short/empty entries crash the upload thread
findings.entry_point: Same untrusted get_level.php lines held in the MyTreasureUserlevelsLoad singleton; reached when the local player presses the editor 'upload' button
findings.sink: String.substring(0, length()-4) on cached server strings; length<4 (e.g. an empty or truncated line) yields negative index -> StringIndexOutOfBoundsException
findings.data_path: MyTreasureEditor.UPLOAD button -> upload() spawns Thread (MyTreasureEditor.java:238-248) -> uploadString() (line 251) -> MyTreasureUserLevels.addLevel(level) (line 120-125) -> isIn(level) -> loop at lines 112-116 calls substring(0, len-4) on EVERY previously downloaded level string. Unlike loadUserlevels(), this Runnable has no surrounding try/catch, so the exception is uncaught on the worker thread and kills the process.
findings.attack_scenario: Attacker plants a degenerate record in the shared level DB (anonymous save_level.php POST of an empty/short value, or truncation introduced by an on-path HTTP modifier). Any player who solves their own editor level and taps 'Upload' thereafter crashes: the dedup scan hits the malformed entry before the POST is issued.
findings.preconditions: At least one level string shorter than 4 chars present in the get_level.php listing AND victim uses the editor upload feature afterwards.
findings.validation_plan: Proxy get_level.php so one 11-line block contains '' as the level line (index i%11==0). In the app, open Editor, build/solve a level (upload button becomes visible after SOLVE succeeds), press Upload; adb logcat shows FATAL EXCEPTION StringIndexOutOfBoundsException originating at MyTreasureUserLevels.isIn.

findings.title: Anonymous, unauthenticated level-submission protocol (no identity, signature, or rate limiting in client)
findings.entry_point: Editor upload path: MyTreasureEditor.touchedButton(UPLOAD) -> upload() thread -> MyTreasureUserLevels.addLevel -> save(level)
findings.sink: Cleartext POST body 'level=<string>' to http://www.apo-games.de/myTreasure/save_level.php (lines 149-163); the request carries no user id, device id, token, or MAC
findings.data_path: The entire authentication/integrity surface is the single 'level=' parameter; the client performs no signing and the protocol offers no field that could identify the submitter, so the server-side DB contents are fully crowd-writable by construction (observable purely from client code).
findings.attack_scenario: curl -d 'level=<anything>' http://www.apo-games.de/myTreasure/save_level.php inserts arbitrary records that are pushed to every client by get_level.php. This is the amplifier that makes findings 02 and 03 remotely exploitable without any network position: one scripted request poisons the shared catalog for all players. It also permits catalog flooding/griefing. (Honest caveat: the missing auth is ultimately a server property; here we can only prove the client neither sends nor requires credentials.)
findings.preconditions: Network access to apo-games.de; knowledge of the fixed endpoint URL hard-coded in MyTreasureConstants.java:13.
findings.validation_plan: tcpdump/mitmproxy a legitimate in-game upload to capture the exact request shape; replay it with curl using an arbitrary level string; reopen the user-levels screen in the app and confirm the forged entry is listed and selectable (pair with the '9999' payload from finding 02 to demonstrate end-to-end impact).

findings.title: Progress/unlock state kept in unauthenticated SharedPreferences; local tampering unlocks difficulty gates
findings.entry_point: Local file /data/data/<pkg>/shared_prefs/MytreasurePref.xml (PREFS_NAME, MyTreasureConstants.java:17), written by saveProperties() and read by loadProperties() (lines 164-184)
findings.sink: curSkulls loaded from prefs (line 173) gates world-map progression checks in MyTreasureMap (NEEDED_SKULLS thresholds at MyTreasureMap.java:92,157,170,182,257,295,332)
findings.data_path: Win -> MyTreasureGame.saveSolvedLevel() (lines 540-562) increments in-memory skulls -> persisted via MyTreasurePanel.saveProperties()/onPauseScreen (lines 186-208, 424-430) -> on next start loadProperties restores them; no checksum/HMAC exists anywhere in the variant (verified: zero MessageDigest/Cipher usage).
findings.attack_scenario: A user with root (or any backup-extraction flow) edits 'skulls' to a large number and relaunches; the temple/pyramid/crypt difficulty tiers unlock without playing. Solved-level markers ('<i>skulls', '<i>level' entries, lines 200-205) are equally editable to fake gold ratings. Purely local cheating; no cross-user effect since this variant transmits no scores.
findings.preconditions: Rooted device or equivalent private-data access; threat model explicitly includes local tampering to cheat.
findings.validation_plan: On a rooted emulator: play briefly, pull /data/data/com.apogames.mytreasure/shared_prefs/MytreasurePref.xml, set name="skulls" to 100, push back, restart app, observe map regions marked locked (skull-count gates) now open and difficulty buttons enabled.

categories_checked_and_absent: remote_code_loading (no ClassLoader/defineClass/DexClassLoader anywhere in the variant; grep over all .java including _from_jar_* trees)
untrusted_deserialization (no ObjectInputStream/XMLDecoder/Serializable reads; saves use SharedPreferences primitives only)
weak_integrity_check (zero MessageDigest/hash usage; MD5-style highscore validation known from desktop siblings is simply absent here - there is no highscore submission at all in this variant)
path_traversal (no java.io File streams, no openFileOutput/getExternalStorage usage in game code; the only persistence is app-private SharedPreferences)

unsafe_native_call (only System.loadLibrary("modplug-"+VERS) at PlayerThread.java:912 inside the vendored andmodplug library, loading a fixed-name lib shipped in the APK; moreover com.peculiargames.* and com.leff.* are not imported by any game source file - the _from_jar_* directories are dead code in this snapshot)
resource_exhaustion (parser dimensions are limited to two digits each, bounding allocation to int[198][99]; the solver MyTreasureSolve caps search at MAX=17 steps)
credential_or_secret_exposure (no API keys, no licensing/AdMob identifiers in source, no account data)
information_disclosure (the only outbound data is the self-authored level string; no device identifiers, location, or PII leave the device)
legacy_sandbox_assumption (no applet entry points, no java.security manager assumptions; Android-only BitsApp entry)
notes: Source root nests the project under 'Users/eliahilse/...' inside the corpus directory; all paths above are relative to the stated SOURCE ROOT. The engine (net.gliblybits.bitsengine.*) and its manifest/assets are external to this snapshot, so engine-side handling of exceptions thrown from think()/onDrawFrame could not be inspected; however, loadLevel() is invoked from the update loop (MyTreasureGame.java:286) with no try/catch in any caller up to the engine boundary, making the crash path of finding 02 robust to review gaps. Network work is correctly off the GL thread (load: MyTreasurePanel.java:390-398; upload: MyTreasureEditor.java:242-247). An honest client can only upload well-formed level strings (generated by MyTreasureEditor.getLevelString(), lines 143-175), which is why malformed-content attacks require the anonymous-scripted-upload or on-path-tampering routes documented above. Compared with desktop siblings of this corpus, this variant lacks: class loading, ObjectInputStream, MD5/highscore logic, custom binary formats (.cheat/.mar/.rep), and JNI paths of its own - its attack surface is essentially the HTTP user-level channel plus local preference tampering.
